steps.context: This step answers the research question directly. Input is the ranked vector from T1S1 derived from the DESeq2 treated-vs-control contrast on human psoriasis lesional vs control skin. Psoriasis lesional skin has a strong, well-characterised expected signature (interferon and TNF/NF-kB inflammatory programmes, IL-6/JAK/STAT3, complement, keratinocyte proliferation), so the results carry a built-in plausibility check — a result with no inflammatory hallmark up should prompt a check of the contrast direction rather than a novel interpretation.
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB hallmark pathways are significantly enriched, and in which direction, in psoriasis lesional (treated) versus control skin?
constraints: Use the human (Homo sapiens, HGNC symbol) hallmark gene set collection — match the organism of the data; do not substitute the mouse hallmark sets or a GO collection.
Restrict every gene set to the genes present in the ranked background before testing, and report the resulting set size alongside the original.
minSize 10, maxSize 500, BH correction across the 50 hallmark sets, fixed random seed.
Report NES with its sign convention stated explicitly (positive = higher in treated/lesional).
Flag hallmarks whose background coverage is below ~40% of their full membership as low-confidence.

If the hallmark gene sets cannot be resolved in the reference store, stop and report that rather than substituting a different collection — the research question is specifically about hallmark pathways.
steps.description: Run preranked gene set enrichment analysis of the T1S1 ranked list against the human hallmark gene set collection (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols — resolve it from the reference store; the human hallmark GMT is the required resource, not the mouse one and not the GO or oncogenic collections). Use fgsea (multilevel) in R or gseapy.prerank in Python — both are installed. Set a minimum set size of 10 and a maximum of 500 genes after restricting each set to the ranked background, and use a fixed random seed for reproducibility. Apply Benjamini-Hochberg correction across the 50 sets. Produce: (a) a results table with pathway, NES, nominal p, BH-adjusted p, set size after background restriction, the fraction of the original hallmark set covered by the 12,000-gene background, and leading-edge genes; (b) a bar or dot plot of significant hallmarks (padj<0.05) ordered by NES, coloured by direction; (c) GSEA enrichment curves for the top 5 up and top 5 down hallmarks; (d) a plain-language summary naming which hallmarks are up in lesional and which are down, with the leading-edge genes that drive each of the top calls. acceptance_criteria: A hallmark results table covering all testable hallmark sets, with NES, nominal p, BH-adjusted p, set size, coverage fraction and leading-edge genes.
Significant hallmarks (padj<0.05) are listed by direction, with the NES sign convention stated.
Bar/dot plot of significant hallmarks and enrichment curves for the top 5 up and top 5 down are written as image artifacts.
Coverage is reported per hallmark and low-coverage sets are flagged.
If no hallmark reaches padj<0.05, that is reported as the finding, with the top-ranked sets by nominal p shown and the result described as null rather than dressed up.

steps.name: Low-depth-sample sensitivity of hallmark calls
caveats: Excluding sample_01 leaves 5 vs 6, which is underpowered even by the standards of the original design — a hallmark losing significance after exclusion may reflect lost power rather than a real artefact, and the NES concordance is the more informative readout than the p-value.

If the recomputed and supplied statistics disagree substantially, the supplied table may have been produced with a different design, filtering, or length correction; report the discrepancy rather than assuming either is correct.
Do not use this step to select a 'better' answer — its output qualifies confidence in T1S2, which remains the primary result.
steps.context: The data profile flags sample_01 at roughly a quarter of the median library size. In a 6-vs-6 unpaired single-batch design, one low-depth sample can materially move a DESeq2 contrast — size-factor estimation and dispersion shrinkage both degrade, and the affected group's within-group variance inflates. Salmon-derived counts may or may not carry a length correction per the data profile; if the recomputed statistics correlate poorly with the supplied table, that discrepancy is a candidate explanation and should be reported rather than silently resolved.
steps.question: Do the hallmark enrichment calls survive exclusion of sample_01, whose library size is ~4x below the median, and is the supplied de_results.csv reproducible from counts.csv?
constraints: Use the counts matrix and metadata as delivered; do not drop genes beyond a minimal low-count prefilter, and state the prefilter used.
Use design ~condition with control as the reference level, so that positive log2FC means higher in treated/lesional — matching the T1S2 sign convention.
Run hallmark GSEA with identical gene sets, minSize, maxSize and seed as T1S2 so the comparison is like-for-like.
Report Spearman correlation between recomputed and supplied Wald statistics, and do NOT overwrite or replace the supplied de_results.csv.
Frame the output as a sensitivity check qualifying T1S2's confidence, not as a replacement primary result.
steps.description: Test whether the hallmark result from T1S2 is robust to the one flagged sample. Load /eval-four-models-v2-without-enrichment-only-ranked-s1-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 genes x 12 samples plus gene column) and /eval-four-models-v2-without-enrichment-only-ranked-s1-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv (12 rows, sample and condition). First report per-sample library sizes and confirm the magnitude of the sample_01 depth deficit, and note which group it belongs to. Then run three things: (1) DESeq2/PyDESeq2 treated-vs-control on all 12 samples with the default design ~condition, and correlate the resulting Wald statistics against the supplied de_results.csv statistics to check the delivered table is reproducible from these inputs — report Spearman rho and the number of genes compared; (2) the same contrast with sample_01 excluded (5 vs 6); (3) hallmark preranked GSEA on both rankings, using the same human hallmark sets, minSize/maxSize and seed as T1S2. acceptance_criteria: Per-sample library sizes are reported and sample_01's deficit and group membership are stated.
Spearman rho between recomputed and supplied DE statistics is reported with the number of genes compared; a rho below ~0.9 is explicitly flagged as a discrepancy needing explanation.
A side-by-side hallmark NES/padj table for primary, full-recomputed, and sample_01-excluded analyses is produced, with the cross-analysis NES rank correlation.
Each hallmark significant in T1S2 is labelled stable or sample_01-dependent.

plan.title: Hallmark GSEA of psoriasis lesional vs control
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question is narrow: which MSigDB hallmark pathways change between the treated (psoriasis lesional) and control skin samples. Differential expression is already done and delivered as /data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns: gene, base_mean, log2_fold_change, log2_fold_change_se, stat, pvalue, padj-style fields), so no re-running of DESeq2 is planned. The analysis therefore reduces to (T1S1) sanity-checking and ranking the supplied DE table into a single, well-behaved gene-level ranking, then (T1S2) running preranked GSEA against the 50 human hallmark sets, then (T1S3) confirming the leading hallmark calls are not an artefact of the one sample flagged in the profile.

Step T1S1 is deliberately not a 'data exploration' step: it produces the ranking vector that GSEA consumes, and it must make the ranking decisions explicit. The DE table is the DESeq2 treated-vs-control contrast; the correct preranked statistic is the Wald `stat` column when present, because it already folds effect size and its standard error together and is stable for low-count genes, whereas raw log2FC alone over-ranks noisy low-expression genes. If `stat` is absent or degenerate, the fallback is sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue), and the choice actually used must be reported. Genes with NA statistics (DESeq2 independent-filtering / outlier rows) are dropped rather than imputed, duplicate gene symbols are collapsed to the single most extreme statistic, and the identifier space must be checked against HGNC symbols because the hallmark GMT is symbol-keyed — an Ensembl-ID index would silently produce zero overlap and an all-null GSEA.

Step T1S2 is the answer to the question. Preranked GSEA (fgsea multilevel, or gseapy prerank) over the 50 HALLMARK_* sets, BH-adjusted across the 50 sets, reporting NES, adjusted p, set size after restriction to the tested background, and leading-edge genes. Only ~12,000 genes were quantified, so hallmark sets will be partially covered; coverage per set must be reported alongside the result, since a hallmark represented by 20 of its 200 members is a weak call regardless of its p-value. GSEA is used rather than an over-representation test on a thresholded DE list because the question asks which pathways *change*, which is directional and does not require a significance cutoff on individual genes.

Step T1S3 is the robustness check the data profile demands. sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which is a real QC concern in a 6-vs-6 unpaired design: at n=6 per group a single low-depth sample can shift the contrast that produced the supplied DE table. This step recomputes the treated-vs-control contrast from /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv (12,000 x 13, gene column plus 12 samples) with DESeq2/PyDESeq2 both with and without sample_01, re-runs hallmark GSEA on each ranking, and reports the concordance of hallmark NES with the primary result. It also verifies that the supplied de_results.csv is reproducible from the counts, which is the only available check on whether the delivered table matches these inputs. Its purpose is to qualify the confidence of the T1S2 calls, not to replace them.

All steps use the staged human hallmark gene sets (MSigDB 2026.1, 50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols), matched to the Homo sapiens origin of the data. fgsea, gseapy, decoupler and clusterProfiler are all present in the sandbox; msigdbr is not, so gene sets must be read from the staged GMT rather than fetched from a package.
